source_text: Sed si de peccati traduce loquebatur, nusquam congruentius diceret: Ideo pertransiit peccatum, quia omnes sunt de coniugum voluptate generati; et adderet: In eo transit, in quo ex tabida primi hominis carne fluxerunt Commendat, inquit, suam caritatem Deus in nobis, quoniam cum adhuc peccatores essemus, Christus pro nobis mortuus est; multo magis iustificati nunc in sanguine ipsius, salvi erimus ab ira per ipsum
pass_a_gloss: But if about/from of-sin by-transmission loquebatur, nowhere congruentius diceret: for-that-reason pertransiit sin, because all are about/from of-spouses by-pleasure generati; and adderet: in to-that transit, in whither from tabida primi of-the-human in-flesh fluxerunt Commendat, he-says, his-own caritatem God in to-us, quoniam when/with still sinners to-be, Christ for to-us dead is; multo more iustificati now in sanguine of-himself, salvi will-be from anger through itself.

lemmas.lexica: LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: But if he was speaking about the transmission of sin by descent, nowhere would it have been more appropriate for him to say, ‘Sin passed to all for this reason: because all were begotten through married people’s pleasure.’ He would have added, ‘It passes in this way: they flowed from the decaying flesh of the first man.’

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
